properties.name: A Decision left proposed AND assigned to somebody is reported by the loop; one nobody was asked to decide stays quiet
properties.statement:
Raised by @ajs from flo2, 2026-08-05, and this is the concrete instance that exposed req:the-loop-says-what-is-owed-to-a-person. A design can hold any number of Decision nodes at proposed — genuinely open choices, one of them blocking another person's work — and NOTHING REPORTS THEM.

MEASURED TWICE, ON TWO DESIGNS, INDEPENDENTLY. (1) On flo2's own design, holding EIGHT proposed decisions: detect_gaps returned 12 gaps, NONE referencing a Decision; loop_status reported unanswered_questions 0, unwritten_answers 0, and has no field that counts an open decision at all. (2) REPRODUCED ON REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN, 2026-08-05, deliberately as a test rather than by accident: capturing this proposal created dec:one-process-many-stores at status proposed and gave it an AUTHORED_BY edge with role=approver to who:ajs — the exact shape this requirement says should be reported. loop_status then returned clean:false with unsurfaced_gaps 11, unanswered_questions 0, and NO field counting an open decision; detect_gaps returned 11 gaps of which ZERO referenced dec:one-process-many-stores. Every one of the 11 was about the capabilities and requirements captured alongside it. So the loop reported eleven things it was owed and stayed silent about the one item a named person had actually been asked to decide.

That second measurement matters more than the first: it is on the design of the tool itself, made by the tool's own instrumentation, on a node built specifically to be the positive case. The detector is not failing on an exotic shape — it is silent on the canonical one.

THE QUIET IS RIGHT; THE LACK OF AN EXIT IS NOT. This is documented and deliberate. The brainstorm skill records a musing as a proposed Decision with its options in prose precisely so the loop stays silent while somebody is still thinking, and detect_gaps fires undecided_decision_point only on a Decision holding two or more REGISTERED ALTERNATIVES — a fork with real design behind each branch. That line is a good one and must survive: a brainstormed Decision with no approver must keep costing nothing, so thinking out loud stays free.

THE PROBLEM IS THAT THERE IS NO WAY TO CROSS IT. A musing that becomes a live question owned by a named person has no state to move to. register_alternative does not fit: it requires a LOCATION per alternative — where that alternative's design export lives, branch-by-file — and the options here are prose ("connect the user's own git repo" against "provision a hosted sandbox"), neither of which has a design export. Using it would mean inventing file paths that do not exist in order to make a detector notice something true. And the Question machinery cannot be pointed at a Decision: answer_question refuses unless gap_to_prompt already recorded a question, and gap_to_prompt takes a GapCandidate from detect_gaps, so Questions are GAP-DERIVED ONLY — there is no way to raise a standalone question against a node somebody must decide on. That refusal is correct and well-explained; the limitation is upstream of it.

THE GRAPH ALREADY KNOWS, which is what makes this cheaper than it looks: AUTHORED_BY with role=approver is already the graph SAYING that a named contributor owes an answer here. The information is present and structured. Nothing computes on it.

THE DISCRIMINATOR THIS REQUIREMENT ASKS FOR: proposed AND carrying an approver edge means somebody has been asked to decide and the loop should say so. Proposed with no approver means somebody is thinking, and the loop stays silent. The graph already distinguishes these two; the loop does not read the distinction.

WHAT IT COST, which is the shape of what it will cost users: flo2's requirement was that its open decisions surface for the second contributor when he clones. The graph could not satisfy it, so it was met OUTSIDE THE GRAPH — a hand-written list in README.md plus a committed loop-nudge hook. That list is a second copy of something the graph already holds, maintained by hand, with nothing checking the two agree. It will drift the first time a decision is added or settled, and it will drift SILENTLY — the precise failure mode reflow2 exists to prevent. A design brain that holds the open decisions but cannot report them pushes its users into keeping a shadow list.
